import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_8/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_8/training_1.csv"

# Load Source 0: detailed student-level scores including school_name and math_score
# index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column as per Hint 24
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1: school-level info, not directly needed for target columns but must be used
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Transformation plan:
# Target schema: ['school_name': string, 'math_score': integer]
# Target examples show math_score is a large integer, much bigger than individual student scores.
# Source0 has math_score per student, Source1 has no math_score.
# So we need to aggregate Source0 math_score by school_name (sum) to get total math_score per school.
# Source1 has school_name and other info but no math_score, so it can be used to ensure all schools are included.
# Join Source1 with aggregated Source0 on school_name to ensure all schools from Source1 appear.
# For schools in Source1 but not in Source0, math_score will be NaN, fill with 0.
# Finally, select columns school_name and math_score (int).

# Aggregate Source0 math_score by school_name (sum)
agg_math_scores = df_source0.groupby('school_name', as_index=False)['math_score'].sum()

# Join aggregated math scores with Source1 on school_name (left join to keep all schools in Source1)
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source1[['school_name']], agg_math_scores, on='school_name', how='left')

# Fill NaN math_score with 0 (schools with no students in Source0)
df_joined['math_score'] = df_joined['math_score'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Final target dataframe with required columns and types
target_df = df_joined[['school_name', 'math_score']]

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_8/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
